fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled per-character bidi types (derived from the fuzzer input code points) are run-length encoded into the linked run list; every subsequent phase operates on these runs, including isolate_level stamping, isolate-chain construction and compaction.

During X1-X8 each run is stamped with the current isolate level. A long prefix of LRI isolates together with an RLO override and overflowing LRI/PDI runs saturate the embedding level (125) and produce adjacent runs that share the same resolved level and type but carry different isolate_level values.

After X1-X8 the per-isolate-level next_isolate/prev_isolate links are built. These links are what get corrupted by the misplaced compaction merge: the run holding a stale prev_isolate back-pointer later becomes the source of the dangling dereference.

compact_list merges adjacent runs when only the type, resolved level and bracket property match; it never compares RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL, so two runs that have the same type and level but different isolate levels are merged even though they must remain separate. This is the root cause of the isolate-chain corruption.

The misplaced merge is executed; merge_with_prev frees the second run and rewrites the isolate links of the surviving run, breaking the symmetry of the isolate chain (the surviving run's next_isolate is overwritten while a later run still holds a prev_isolate back-pointer to it).

The merged run's next_isolate is unconditionally overwritten with the second run's successor; because the merged runs had different isolate levels, this orphans the true chain successor (its prev_isolate still points at the surviving run), leaving an asymmetric / stale isolate link.

A later compaction merge (compact_list at the end of the phase) merges a run whose prev_isolate still points to a run that was freed moments earlier by a preceding merge_with_prev call; dereferencing that dangling isolate-link pointer and writing to it is the heap-use-after-free write.

via: same type and level runs at different isolate levels
dangling isolate link to freed run

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: The public issue states that during list compaction two runs with the same type and level but different isolate levels are merged even though they should remain separate, which leaves a dangling isolate-link pointer that is dereferenced during a later merge and causes a heap-use-after-free write. This trace reproduces exactly that: compact_list's merge condition (fribidi-bidi.c:108) lacks the RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL comparison, so runs at different isolate levels are fused; the fusion overwrites the surviving run's next_isolate (merge_with_prev:94) and orphans the chain successor's prev_isolate back-pointer; a subsequent compaction then merges the run holding that stale prev_isolate and writes through it (merge_with_prev:93) into the freed run.
